name: The Tasman, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Hobart

seo.title: The Tasman Hobart Honeymoon Review: Luxury Collection 2026
seo.description: 152-room Luxury Collection waterfront hotel — 2021 opening, three architectural eras. Score 83/100, from $480/night.

content.verdict: The Tasman opened in late 2021 — Hobart's newest serious luxury hotel, occupying three different architectural eras across a single block on the Parliament Square waterfront: an 1840s sandstone heritage building, a 1940s art deco wing, and a contemporary glass-and-stone new build. 152 rooms across the three. The Marriott-owned Luxury Collection brand brings consistent polish that the older Hobart hotels can't match — proper room service, full spa, indoor lap pool, and the city's first hotel cocktail bar (Mary Mary) at international level. The restaurant Peppina by chef Massimo Mele is one of the city's top three. The Tasman is two blocks from the MONA ferry, walking to Salamanca and Battery Point. Caveats: the three-era architecture means rooms vary radically — the heritage rooms (1840s sandstone) have the most character, the new-build rooms have the best views. Service can feel corporate vs the Henry Jones' more personal touch. For honeymooners who prioritize amenity completeness (spa, pool, room service) over heritage character, The Tasman is the most amenity-rich Hobart option.
content.best_room: Heritage Spa Room in the 1840s sandstone building with freestanding bath. Or Pavilion Suite in the new-build wing with the largest harbour view. Avoid Tasman Premium standard rooms — they lack the architectural character that makes this hotel.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Arrival in Hobart
itinerary_7_nights.description: HBA to The Tasman (15 min). Welcome at Mary Mary bar with Tasmanian gin. Settle into Heritage Spa Room. Dinner at Peppina.

itinerary_7_nights.title: MONA day
itinerary_7_nights.description: MONA Roma ferry (5 min walk). Full day at MONA. Return at 4pm. Sunset cocktails at Mary Mary. Dinner at Franklin.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Salamanca and waterfront
itinerary_7_nights.description: Saturday Salamanca Market. Kelly's Steps to Battery Point. Lunch at Jackman & McRoss. Afternoon Mt Wellington. Spa treatment late afternoon. Dinner at Aloft.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Tasman Peninsula
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive to Port Arthur. Pennicott sea-cliff boat tour. Return for spa. Dinner at Brufa.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Bruny Island
itinerary_7_nights.description: Bruny Island full-day. Return at 6pm. Light dinner at Peppina bar.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Whisky day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Tasmanian whisky tour. Lunch at Stillwater. Final dinner at Peppina with chef's tasting menu.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow departure
itinerary_7_nights.description: Breakfast. Spa hammam. HBA for departure.

caveats: Three architectural eras mean rooms vary radically — pick category carefully.
New-build rooms have the best views, heritage rooms the most character — trade-off either way.
152 rooms feels more corporate than Henry Jones or MACq.
Indoor lap pool is small (15m) but functional.
Heritage building rooms have heritage quirks — no air-con in some, request specifically if needed.

faqs.question: Good for honeymooners?
faqs.answer: Very good — most amenity-complete Hobart hotel. Best spa and only indoor pool of the waterfront options.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: Year-round viable; December–March for summer Hobart, June for Dark Mofo, April–May for autumn.

faqs.question: Book in advance?
faqs.answer: 2–3 months for Heritage Spa Rooms and Pavilion Suites.

faqs.question: Best room type?
faqs.answer: Heritage Spa Room or Pavilion Suite. Avoid Tasman Premium.
